result:
There is a specific kind of magic found only in the pre-dawn hours. It exists in the liminal space between the comfort of sleep and the demands of the day. Before the birds decide to sing, and before the cars begin to rattle, there is only the low hum of the refrigerator and the quiet sound of the house settling into itself.

I love walking through this quiet. It feels less like waiting and more like preparation. The coffee kettle begins its simmer, a metallic whisper signaling change is imminent. Outside, streetlights cast long halos on the driveway, fading against the gray morning sky. The air inside is cool, heavy with the scent of yesterday’s rain.

In these moments, the world feels fragile. It is a secret between the few awake. There is no rush to prove oneself, no inbox to conquer, no notifications to drown out thoughts rising from the deep end. It is a permission slip to just be, rather than do.

Yet, this stillness is temporary. The sky will bruise purple before turning that familiar blue. The stove will demand attention. But I keep this ritual because I know the noise will come soon enough. To hoard a pocket of silence is to stockpile peace for the storm ahead. It allows me to face the chaos steadily, carrying a fragment of this quiet back into the busy world.

That is why I wait for the dawn. Not for the sun, but for the breath before the song.
